label: bluegecko-3v1-cape-violet
people: [gecko]thebluegecko (lobby skill 34.3 in the record header), Armada, alone in the west box with his start at B3. His only line was 'gl hf!' at 0:28 (bot.log: player 0). The user, as computer_whisperer, hosted from the host's seat and typed four comments (see user_comments).
our_side: Three seats of ours on the east edge, all Armada (the lobby side was 'random'): t1 orange at H6 (record-0), t2 sky blue at H4 (record-1), t3 green at H2 (record-2). One player, claude-opus-5-5 at effort medium (Claude Code 2.1.283), over all three seats, with no commander role. The hands were Jev jev-1.13.0, and the decompression stage was on. This was before the 2026-10-02 hands rebuild. Realtime, in the user's lobby, on a map new to us.
summary: thebluegecko opened as greedily as a person can: two Pawns were his only army until his first Welder at 7:41, he reclaimed his bot lab at 5:12 and both shipyards for an advanced bot lab at 6:58, and his construction ships took the sea (16 extractors under water by 8:00, 24 by 10:00). We took none of the map's 26 underwater spots, because every Beaver step to one was skipped as 'not free' and every shipyard order snapped to land; both were picture defects, fixed the next day in b9a43ff. Our three seats' combined army was 3.0k, 6.9k and 11.7k against his 108, 108 and 1,158 at 4, 6 and 8 minutes, but all three Rovers turned home at 2:41-2:53 and the player held and then gathered the groups in our half (3:56-7:57) instead of crossing. The commit reached his base strung out at 8:35, met five Welders, two Beamers and an LLT, and lost 6.7k while killing two Welders (700). From then on his sea extractors and reclaim-fed income outgrew us (40 extractors to our 29 at 10:00), and our Stouts broke Welder pushes at spot_29 but lost every advance through the E3 neck. His army grew from 4.3k at 10:00 to 18.5k at 16:00, and Liches from air plants we never saw killed all three commanders at 17:19, 17:29 and 18:18.

root.what: At 3:56 the player read 'army 2.7k vs 54 seen' and ordered the three groups to stand together at the D2 choke and hold, advancing only once they had gathered. His base had been unseen since 2:41-2:53, when the hands' pick sent each seat's Rover home on sighting a constructor and a Pawn about 700 from his start. His whole army until 7:41 was two Pawns, an LLT, a commander and one or two Beamers, and from 5:12 to 7:22 he had no land factory. The window was 3:00-8:00, at 3.6-35x on seat 0 alone. It was spent in our half: the gather stalled, and the commit landed after his Welders. Everything after 8:35 is its cost.

Nothing crossed while his army was two Pawns, and he had no land factory from 5:12. A stronger player sends the first handful across at about 2:30-3:00 and the whole army by 4:00-5:00, to kill his constructors, extractors and lab.

their_play: Armada bots from B3. He opened with four wind turbines before the lab at 0:34, two constructors, LLTs at 1:06 and 2:28, and two Pawns (1:39, 1:49), which were his whole army until 7:41. He expanded hard: 12 extractors at 4:00 and 18 at 6:00 on land, plus geothermals from 4:20 and metal makers from 5:18. Shipyards at 4:21 (B4) and 5:15 (B2) made construction ships from 5:13, and they took the sea: 16 extractors under water by 8:00 and 24 by 10:00, eight of them on our side at E3-G7 (8:12-11:00). He reclaimed his bot lab at 5:12 and both shipyards (6:50, 7:42) and went straight to an advanced bot lab at 6:58, with a moho at 7:34. His Welders came from 7:41: 3 at 8:00, 12 at 10:00, 24 at 14:00. Two Beamers (4:38, 6:30) and an LLT covered his base. He met our strung-out Blitz column in that base at 8:35-9:03 and lost two Welders. His metal income went from 68 at 8:00 to 273 at 10:00 (the replay card's figure; my reading is that it was the reclaim of our wrecks at B3). From 10:00 Welders and Farks pushed through D3 and the E3 neck, and from 14:00 they wore our Stouts down in our half. He added an air plant at 9:53 (A3), an advanced air plant at 12:11 (A2), a Dreadnought seen at 13:32 and Longbow cruisers on the coasts. Six Liches with radar planes killed our three commanders from 17:19 to 18:18. He said nothing during the game beyond 'gl hf!'.

bears_on.note: This is the lesson's 'extremely greedy economic opening': two Pawns until 7:41, no land factory 5:12-7:22, 18 extractors at 6:00. Our first Blitzes stood as pickets at home (0:00 packet) and nothing crossed to press him.
Our combined army was 28x his at 4:00 and 64x at 6:00 (card: 3,046 and 6,896 against 108). It went unused until 7:57 and was spent at 8:35 against his new tier 2.
The commit arrived strung out (17 of 48 at B3 at 8:36; group_A_t2 still at d2_gate). At 10:20-11:00 t2 fought alone while t1 and t3 huddled at spot_19. The player's note at 11:47: 't1 fought alone'.
The game was lost on extractors. We led on land (28 to 15 at 8:00), but all his growth from 6:00 was under water: 40 to 29 at 10:00, 45 to 22 at 14:00. The Welder fights were the symptom.
Here half the map was the sea: 26 of 72 spots lie under water, and we held none.
A person reclaimed his tier-1 bot lab (5:12) and both shipyards (6:50, 7:42) to pay for the advanced bot lab (6:58), and made no tier-1 soldiers beyond two Pawns.

Our Blitz mass sat in our half from 3:00 to 7:40, which made his factory-less tier-2 sprint safe. What we did with the units told him what he could get away with, as in the lesson's 'you made many lashers, so I was safe to go T2'.
My reading, unproven: his income went from 68 at 8:00 to 273 at 10:00 after 6.7k of ours died at his base. Our 13:09 plan to reclaim about 8k of wrecks at D3 never held D3.

lens.existing_review: no review.md; three model reviews in 00/: posing-review.md, topology-review.md, decompression-review.md
lens.caveats: The match has no truth file. The re-simulated replay /ceph/christian/within-reason/run/matches-archive/1790483222-replay-human-cape-violet supplies truth-1..3 with the live game's unit ids (our commander is 11775 in both), so his numbers are true, not floors. The per-match tools read record-0 only, so seats 1-2 were read through scratchpad directories of symlinks. On truth, analyze_match counts his reclaimed buildings (armlab 5:12, armsy 6:50, 7:42) as losses. The sea count maps each extractor to its nearest spot (it reads 27 for 26 at 14:00). The 273 income at 10:00 is the card's figure, with reclaim not separated. chat.jsonl marks all four comments '?'; bot.log gives player 3 (the host's seat) without the [WReason] prefix, which design §6 rules are the user's. pro_baseline was not run (Comet only), nor was impedance_sweep. That a push at 4:00-6:00 would have won is my reading; his commander and D-gun are unpriced. Where I differ from the model reviews and the ledger: (1) posing-review ranks by cost (21.8k to Welders first); this row ranks by root, the 3:00-8:00 window against a factory-less opponent, which those reviews could not see without a truth file. (2) The B3 push killed 700 (two Welders), not 2.1k. (3) Liches killed three commanders (17:19, 17:29, 18:18), not two. The ledger's and the reviews' other findings stand.

open_questions: Would a crossing at 4:00-5:00 (about 30 Blitzes against two Pawns, an LLT, a Beamer being built and his commander) have killed his lab and constructors, or did the D-gun make it a trade?
Was his income jump from 68 (8:00) to 273 (10:00) the reclaim of our 6.7k at B3? The card does not separate reclaim.

Why did the pick send every Rover home at about 0.6 on sighting one constructor and one Pawn, 700 from his start? Was it the old scout state ending on any sighting? Review item F6 names the same at player-9.
With the sea spots listed, would the Beavers have taken them before his construction ships arrived (8:12 on our side), and would the player have sent the amphibious commanders?
spot_12 is an island (+73), not under water, yet seat 2's Beaver skipped it as 'not free' too. Was that the same defect, or reach by class?
The backlog's episode index tags this game with group O. The 'without reach' half was already in this build (d265666 is H-HANDS-ODDS-REACH); what bit was the odds by metal and tier (afc08b6).
